summary: 14-day Nightscout analysis demonstrates excellent overall glycemic control with an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) of 0.0%, and a low Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%. Basal rates, CR, ISF, and AAPS automation parameters are well-balanced. Minor postprandial excursions during weekend brunch (peaks up to 188 mg/dL) are safely managed by UAM and SMB delivery, and can be further minimized by optimizing bolus timing rather than adjusting core profile parameters.

analysis_steps.findings: 1,345 CGM readings collected across 14 days with 100% data coverage, zero gaps, and an average cadence of 15.0 minutes. Complete active AAPS profile and treatment logs provided.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries, 0 gaps, 0 duplicates, active AAPS profile with basal, ISF, CR, target, and DIA defined.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Raw per-5-minute loop state decision traces are summarized via telemetry aggregate summaries.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic stability is exceptional with zero time spent below 70 mg/dL and 0.3% time above 180 mg/dL. Glucose variability is very low (CV 12.9%).
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%, TAR 0.3%, nocturnal minima touching 70-71 mg/dL on isolated days (Aug 11, Aug 17).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific activity logs preceding isolated 03:00 BG dips.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal segments (0.85 to 1.05 U/h) hold overnight and fasting glucose within target ranges (95-110 mg/dL overnight; 90-105 mg/dL morning). Isolated 03:00 dips to 70-71 mg/dL reflect lingering late-dinner IOB rather than true basal excess.
Carb ratios (9-12 g/U) and ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U) effectively return glucose to target by hours 4-6 post-meal. DIA of 5.5 hours aligns with modern rapid-acting insulin pharmacodynamics.
analysis_steps.evidence: 4-hour postprandial BG returns to baseline across all recurring meal windows (breakfast, brunch, dinner) without late hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Isolated correction boluses without carbs to independently verify ISF segments.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and functioning safely. Delivery parameters (3-min interval, 45-min max SMB basal, 30-min max UAM basal) assist postprandial recovery smoothly without causing over-basalization.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3, max_smb_basal_minutes=45, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30. TBR remains 0.0%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Explicit SMB activation condition UI toggles are unpopulated in JSON export metadata.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (Max Basal 2.4 U/h, Max IOB 8.0 U) provide appropriate ceiling protection relative to TDD (~10 U/day) and average boluses (4.2-5.8 U). Dynamic ISF factor at 100% maintains predictable scaling.

Weekday breakfast (42g, 4.2U, 20-min prebolus, 70% immediate) and dinner (54g, 5.5U) yield stable control. Weekend brunch (68g, 5.8U, 10-min prebolus, 60% immediate, 20g e-carbs) experiences higher 2-hour peaks (188 mg/dL) due to delayed initial insulin delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows show 2-hour BG rise of +62 to +70 mg/dL for weekend brunch versus +33 to +57 mg/dL for weekday breakfast.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Execution logs for exact per-meal prebolus timing.

analysis_steps.findings: The 20g e-carbs declaration over 120 minutes for weekend brunch accurately models high-fat/protein absorption, preventing late-tail hypoglycemia at hours 4-6.
analysis_steps.evidence: Brunch 4-hour BG averages 115 mg/dL and 6-hour BG averages 111-113 mg/dL, confirming overall insulin amount and e-carb absorption model match real absorption.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Detailed macronutrient breakdowns beyond declared meal context notes.

analysis_steps.findings: Core profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) are optimized and should be maintained. The observed post-brunch peak is an execution timing issue best resolved by increasing prebolus time or upfront bolus percentage rather than changing CR or basal rates.
analysis_steps.evidence: High overall TIR (99.7%), zero TBR, clean 4-hour postprandial recoveries across all meal windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None preventing a complete synthesis and recommendation plan.

strengths: Exceptional Time-in-Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL).
Highly predictable glucose profile with a low Coefficient of Variation (12.9%).
Accurately configured Basal, CR, and ISF profiles that achieve full postprandial glucose recovery by hour 4.
Appropriately configured AAPS safety limits (Max Basal 2.4 U/h, Max IOB 8.0 U) preventing insulin stacking.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose peaks up to 188 mg/dL during weekend brunch due to a shortened prebolus (10 min) and lower upfront bolus percentage (60%).

recommendations.title: Optimize Weekend Brunch Bolus Timing
recommendations.description: Increase prebolus duration for weekend brunch from 10 minutes to 20 minutes, or increase immediate bolus percentage from 60% to 70%, while keeping the 20g e-carbs entry over 120 minutes to flatten the 2-hour peak (188 mg/dL) without causing late hypoglycemia.

recommendations.description: Confirm in AAPS preferences that SMB activation conditions (e.g., SMB with COB, SMB always) are explicitly toggled as intended, as these UI flags were unpopulated in the export file.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Glycemic metrics are optimal (99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV) and postprandial glucose recovers fully to baseline across all time windows, confirming profile accuracy.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Perform a periodic clean overnight fasting check (00:00-06:00) without late evening meals to confirm 0.85 U/h basal stability.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Continue administering a 15-20 minute prebolus with 70-100% immediate bolus for standard meals, allowing SMB and UAM to absorb minor absorption variations. For high-fat weekend brunch, increase prebolus from 10 to 20 minutes while maintaining 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Total insulin dosage (CR 10-11 g/U) is accurate as evidenced by 4-hour recovery to baseline, but early carb surge outpaces insulin availability during weekend brunch.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe 2-hour postprandial glucose during the next weekend brunch with a 20-minute prebolus.

exceptions.suggestion: Extend prebolus duration from 10 minutes to 20 minutes, or increase immediate bolus share from 60% to 70%, keeping 20g e-carbs (120 min duration, 15 min offset).
exceptions.rationale: Reduces peak glucose excursion from 188 mg/dL to below 160 mg/dL without changing total insulin or causing late-tail hypoglycemia.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Keep all core profile parameters (Basal, CR, ISF, Targets, DIA) exactly as currently configured.
Step 2: On the next weekend brunch, test extending prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 20 minutes before eating.
Step 3: Monitor 2-hour and 4-hour postprandial glucose to verify reduced peak excursion while confirming 4-hour stability.
Step 4: Confirm in AAPS preferences that SMB and Autosens feature toggles match your intended setup.
education: A 4-hour postprandial glucose return to baseline indicates that the Carb Ratio (CR) is accurate, even if a 2-hour peak occurs.
When 2-hour postprandial peaks occur despite correct 4-hour recovery, the cause is usually bolus timing (prebolus duration or upfront fraction) rather than a defective CR.
Extended carbs (e-carbs) in AAPS model delayed macronutrient absorption in the loop software without delivering a pump extended bolus.
safety_notes: Decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their care team.
Make changes one at a time and closely monitor glucose trends, particularly after changing meal timing or profile settings.
Ensure hypoglycemia treatment resources are accessible at all times.
